messages:
From: Ryan Sullivan <ryan.sullivan@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden spike in timeouts and 5xxs — sample logs attached

Logan —

We started seeing a dramatic increase in completion timeouts and 500s around 09:00 PST for the checkout personalization calls. Impact: a) ~12% of requests are timing out after 20s, b) a correlated jump in 5xxs. The attached sample shows both timeouts and internal errors (request IDs included).

This is affecting our payment conversion on a few high-traffic pages. Can you triage and tell us expected ETA for mitigation? We need something faster than a week.

Request IDs: acme-req-9a1b, acme-req-9a1c, acme-req-9a1f (see file).

Thanks,
Ryan Sullivan
Head of Engineering — Acme Commerce

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-25T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in timeouts and 5xxs — rapid response request

Ryan —

Thanks for the alert and the logs. Sorry you're seeing this. We're pulling a rapid-response here and will prioritize a short-term mitigation plus a root-cause follow-up.

Immediate asks for your side:
- If you can identify a representative request id that reproduces the issue consistently, reply with it; our traces will look for that.
- Confirm whether this traffic is coming from a single region/route.

Planned immediate actions (internal):
- Karthik: running traces & checking worker queue depth + concurrency caps.
- Marissa: drafting a mutual action plan and proposing a short exec call to align on credits and timeline.
- Grace: will clear escalation for a temporary capacity bump if we need it.

I'll stay on this thread and update every 30 minutes until we have a mitigation.

— Logan
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-25T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in timeouts and 5xxs — rapid response request

Team — quick findings from the first 20m trace window:
- Observed pronounced queueing on the model-worker tier serving Acme's routing key. Worker pool avg queue length jumped from ~4 -> ~72 in ~6 minutes.
- Per-node concurrency cap sitting at 256; overall request arrival rate briefly exceeded pooled capacity leading to request drop/retries and cascading KV cache misses.
- Majority of long tails show heavy decoder time (50–90% of CPU on a few workers), not network.

Immediate mitigation recommendations (order matters):
1) Temporary routing change: route Acme traffic to a dedicated pool with relaxed concurrency caps (temp increase to 384/node) — requires Grace approval. Expected impact: drops queue depth within 5–10 minutes.
2) Activate prefix-only KV cache for checkout prompts to reduce decode load for repeated prefixes. Expected: ~30% token CPU reduction.
3) Fallback policy: if decode time > 12s, fall back to a slightly smaller model (same family) for that request path. Low-latency but slightly lower quality.

I've attached a trace slice that highlights the worker hot-spots.

Attachment: trace_slice_0912.json (stub)

Karthik
Sr. SRE — Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Sullivan <ryan.sullivan@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & short-term remediation proposal

Ryan —

Appreciate the heads-up. We're putting a short mutual action plan together so Acme has clarity on steps and timelines. Draft plan highlights:
- t+0: Route traffic to dedicated pool (if approved) + temporary concurrency bump.
- t+15m: Enable prefix-KV cache for the checkout model.
- t+45m: Enable fallback to lighter model for >12s decodes.
- t+4h: Post-mitigation telemetry check and decision on longer-term adjustments (quantization profile, sharding).

We can offer a one-time operational credit for the incident window and an expedited engineering review. Would you be available for a 30-min exec/ops sync at 11:00 PST?

Attachment: MAP-Acme-v1.docx (stub)

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Straggler responses & intermittent 5xx — rapid response request

I approve a temporary capacity bump to the dedicated pool for Acme up to 384 concurrent per node for the next 3 hours. Ops will apply the routing change now. Karthik, please monitor queue length and KV cache hit ratio; escalate if we see memory pressure.

Also looping in Evelyn so leadership is aware. If mitigation does not materially reduce customer impact within 60m, we should convene the exec bridge.

— Grace
VP, Product Operations

We'll keep monitoring and will surface any regressions, but this looks resolved for now. Please keep me posted on the post-incident RCA and any permanent configuration changes you recommend.

Ryan
